key_insight: KANEx aims to turn the interpretability of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) into clinically useful explanations for medical imaging, going beyond fluent but shallow text generated by vision-language models. It connects the visual model’s internal structure to explanation generation so clinicians can better understand why a chest X-ray prediction was made.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between prediction accuracy and explainability in medical AI, where chest X-ray classifiers may be accurate but remain black boxes. It also tackles the limitation of current VLM-based explanation systems that produce natural-language rationales without exposing the underlying decision process of the visual model.
method: Uses Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to leverage spline-based, more interpretable components in the image classifier.
Translates model internals into explanation signals that can support medical explainability.
Integrates the interpretability of KANs with chest X-ray analysis to produce explanations that are more grounded in the model’s behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights a path toward explainable medical imaging systems that are both accurate and trustworthy. It is especially relevant for deploying models in clinical settings where transparency, auditability, and clinician confidence are essential.

paper_title: KANEx: Translating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks' Interpretability to Medical Explainability
paper_authors: Krithi Shailya, Ananya Lakshmi Ravi, Venkatanathan K. V., Sowmya S. Sundaram, Gokul S. Krishnan
